root.summary: On 13x13, corners come first, followed by side extensions along the 3rd/4th lines. Unlike 9x9, you cannot fight everywhere at once — build balanced corner-plus-side frameworks.

children.summary: Territory-oriented corner opening. Faces one side faster than 4-4 and invites the opponent to approach on the open side.
White approaches Black's 3-4 stone low on the 3rd line, aiming to slide into the corner or establish a side base.
Black secures the corner solidly while White settles along the bottom side — a classic peaceful 13x13 joseki.
White extends two spaces along the 3rd line to make a living eye-shape base.
Black pinches White's approach stone, denying an easy side base and starting a corner-vs-center fight.
White counter-attacks Black's corner from the left side instead of running straight out.
White approaches on the 4th line to prioritize center influence (moyo) over 3rd-line territory.
Black takes the corner cash while White builds an outward-facing wall.
Balanced influence + speed. Controls the corner in one move while radiating power toward both adjacent sides and the center.
White dives directly into the 3-3 point under Black's 4-4 stone to steal corner territory.
Black blocks on the wider side to build an outer wall while White lives inside the corner.
White turns along the 3rd line to guarantee two eyes; Black gets thick outside influence.
White approaches Black's 4-4 corner from the top side at a 2-space knight's interval.
Black defends the right side and corner simultaneously with a flexible one-space jump.
Playing opposite corners (D4 + K4 or D10 + K4) creates a dynamic Nirensei or cross-fuseki game.
White claims the remaining open corner before side extensions begin.
